correspondence.component_scope: Initial headward feeder southwest of Nova Esperança do Piriá
correspondence.finding: The Nova Esperança original shows the corresponding small channel along the Cabeceira do Piriá/Cabeceira setting, through the Novo Horizonte corridor and northeast toward Nova Esperança do Piriá. This is visually followed as a watercourse, distinct from the red road lines. The locality label Cabeceira do Piriá is not itself treated as a hydronym or a surveyed spring. Separate Igarapé Jipuiuba and Pitrol labels are not transferred to the initial selected channel.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_at_generalized_corridor_scale
correspondence.name_scope_limit: Initial feeder correspondence is established without assigning an individual hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Nova Esperança, Alto Rio Guamá margin and Cristal–Japim corridor
correspondence.finding: The Nova Esperança map traces the connected river northeast through the Água Preta and Sete Barracas setting to Vila do Cristal and Japim. Printed Rio Piriá labels identify the river beside Cristal and Japim. The Igarapé Água Preta, Igarapé Grande and Igarapé Santo Antônio approaches remain distinct tributary settings. Overlapping Viseu cartography follows the same northward channel and the northeast turn toward BR-316 west of Cachoeira do Piriá. The green/brown administrative and protected-area boundaries are not substituted for the watercourse.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_at_generalized_corridor_scale
correspondence.name_scope_limit: Bounded river labels and corridor identity only; no exact headward name-transition point or tributary renaming.

correspondence.component_scope: BR-316 to Curupaiti and the broad lower-river bends
correspondence.finding: The Viseu original overlaps the fragment transition at BR-316 and labels Rio Piriá on the river northwest of Cachoeira do Piriá. It follows the channel north through the Vila Carrapatinho setting to Curupaiti, the BR-308 crossing, Bucuteua and the lower bend beside Porto da Firmiana. The western lateral drainage approaching the Curupaiti corridor remains a tributary; the east-side Gurupi corridor is a separate river. The wide meanders and water-filled side areas in the lower reach are river/estuarine features, not evidence for a separately named lake or reservoir.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_at_generalized_corridor_scale
correspondence.name_scope_limit: The map supports the connected representative river corridor; no name assigned to each unlabelled small tributary or lateral water area.

correspondence.component_scope: São José do Piriá to the Beira Mar do Piriá estuarine approach
correspondence.finding: The Viseu original shows the Rio Piriá-labelled meanders below Porto da Firmiana, the passage beside São José do Piriá and Itaçu, and the continuing channel beside Beira Mar do Piriá and Itamixila. This is the western estuarine river arm, separated from the Rio Gurupi at Viseu town to the east. Several tidal side channels are visible, but the selected northbound corridor remains geographically distinguishable.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_at_generalized_corridor_scale
correspondence.name_scope_limit: Estuarine continuation is included in representative identity. No claim that every lateral tidal branch has the same hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected tidal terminal and Atlantic receiving setting
correspondence.finding: The Viseu original follows the selected continuation east of the Novo Jardim/Ararapá/Conxíndua setting into the wider tidal water west of the Itacupim landmass, with further estuarine water leading to the labelled Oceano Atlântico. Santos and Aviz Figure 1 independently labels this western estuary Piriá River, the eastern estuary Gurupi River and the outer receiving water Atlantic Ocean. The selected terminal is understood at this generalized widening-estuary scale; it is not promoted to an exact outer shoreline or ocean-mouth point.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_at_generalized_corridor_scale
correspondence.name_scope_limit: Piriá estuarine corridor, separate Atlantic receiving water and adjacent Gurupi system; individual tidal-channel names remain null.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward ice opening and northward transition
correspondence.finding: The southern opening and long initial northward approach lie in the mapped ice/perennial-snow setting west of Lambert Land. Farther north the route reaches the ice/exposed-land margin and southern western Kronprins Christian Land, west of the Blåsø and Skallingen setting. The source distinguishes the ice area from bedrock and intervening Quaternary-covered valleys. No named river is established for the long model-aligned opening.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: Ice contours and the selected straight segments are not interpreted as a mapped surface or subglacial river.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward bend and northward western terrain connector
correspondence.finding: The model turns west across the western exposed-land margin south of the Centrum Sø valley, then turns north close to that margin. The full bend, intervening bedrock and small Quaternary-covered valley crossings are visible. The map does not depict these land-crossing model steps as one consistently named natural channel.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: No adjacent geological-unit name, small channel or land label is promoted to a river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward loop and western Centrum Sø valley
correspondence.finding: The middle route makes an eastward and northward loop through the western Skallingen/Kronprins Christian Land terrain and the mapped valley system southwest and west of Centrum Sø. It reaches and crosses the western valley junction associated with Centrum Sø before returning north. The original explicitly distinguishes the lake body to the east, Quaternary-covered valley floors and exposed bedrock on either side.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: Centrum Sø is a distinct lake-context label. The review does not rename the entire selection after the lake or require pointwise agreement with small valley channels.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern inland continuation
correspondence.finding: North of the western Centrum Sø valley the selected route proceeds across the mapped exposed-land belt of Kronprins Christian Land toward its westward turn. The entire interval is visible, with relief, local streams and small lakes differentiated from the broad ice area farther east. There is no unread geographic connector in this interval.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: The apparent model alignment is not accepted as evidence of a continuous natural river across the terrain.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern turn and actual Holbæk Bugt ending
correspondence.finding: After the westward turn the selected corridor continues north along the western exposed-land belt, east of the mapped Fyns Sø/Skjoldungeelv context. Its final northeastward approach reaches the southern inner arm labelled Holbæk Bugt, connected northward to Danmark Fjord near Kap Holbæk and Kap Trend. This is the actual northern terminal setting, distinct from the southern Nioghalvfjerdsfjorden/Lambert Land setting and from Centrum Sø.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: Holbæk Bugt is a bay/fjord-arm context, Fyns Sø is a separate lake, and Skjoldungeelv is a separately labelled neighboring watercourse. None is supported as a representative hydronym for the complete selected modeled route.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward Surumo corridor south of Cerro La Salvación and toward La Introducción
correspondence.finding: The original NB-20-4 geological sheet places the selected western headward setting on the Río Surumo corridor and shows nearby Cerro La Salvación, Corre Gente and La Introducción. Surumo remains separately labeled. The headward setting and broad course are readable; the selected onward northward transition toward Santa María is not established from the finer linework.
correspondence.correspondence: Headward corridor supported; material onward connection pending

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward southern-delta corridor toward Cuyubini
correspondence.finding: The selected eastward course lies along the NB-20-4 corridor labeled Río Santa María, which continues toward the separately labeled Río Cuyubini at the northeastern part of that sheet. Río La Horqueta is a separate tributary corridor to the southeast. The broader SAGECAN map labels Santa Marta along the state-boundary setting but omits the detail needed to settle the preceding Surumo transition. The two Santa-name readings are not silently merged.
correspondence.correspondence: Eastward named corridor and broad Cuyubini relationship read; upstream transition remains pending

correspondence.component_scope: Cuyubini and El Terror transition into the middle northern corridor
correspondence.finding: NB-20-4 and the adjoining NC-20-16 map both show Río Cuyubini crossing their shared northern/southern sheet setting. NC-20-16 labels El Terror on the Cuyubini corridor. The selected route then lies toward the Guayocaicara branch to its west and north, but thin, discontinuous and intersecting source linework does not reliably establish that material connection. This is not treated as proven continuous Cuyubini-to-Guayocaicara flow.
correspondence.correspondence: Cuyubini setting read; material connector to Guayocaicara pending

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Guayocaicara corridor and its lower continuation toward Arature
correspondence.finding: NC-20-16 places the selected middle northward corridor along the labeled Río Guayocaicara and maps its lower bend westward into the Arature delta corridor. Río Ibaruma lies separately to the west. The middle-to-lower corridor is readable, while the connection to the selected southern Cuyubini setting remains pending as described above.
correspondence.correspondence: Named middle and lower continuation read; southern material connection unresolved

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern lower Arature course
correspondence.finding: NC-20-16 labels Caño Arature on the northwest-trending channel followed by the selected lower line. Fundación Empresas Polar lámina 173 independently labels this delta corridor Río Arature. The chapter settlement map also locates Boca de Arature and a settlement associated with Arature in the lower setting. Acure, Imataca and Basama are shown separately and are not substituted for the selected Arature reach.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported lower corridor across the selected FID boundary

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected terminal and receiving channel
correspondence.finding: The original NC-20-16 map and regional hydrography sheet place Arature entering the broad Río Grande/Boca Grande waterway east of the Curiapo and Isla Pagayo setting. This is an internal delta receiving channel of the Orinoco; the Atlantic outlet lies farther east. The selected model sea class is retained as metadata but is not used to claim a direct open-coast mouth.
correspondence.correspondence: Actual terminal setting supported at generalized corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Ticllacocha headwater and Tanta approach
correspondence.finding: The Tanta original depicts the southern Ticllacocha lake complex with a northward outlet. That channel continues past separate eastern lake-fed branches from the Piscococha and Chuspicocha settings to Tanta. The selected geometry uses this southern approach rather than the northwestern lake chain. The tourism inventory independently identifies Ticllacocha as the Cañete source setting, but the geographic correspondence rests on the original map.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Paucarcocha and the eastward upper bend
correspondence.finding: North of Tanta the mapped channel reaches Laguna Paucarcocha. The original distinguishes the elongated lake from the northwestern and northern incoming drainage, then traces the connecting river east toward Vilca. The study identifies Paucarcocha as an impounded upper-basin lake and describes its outlet/spillway; its Figure 3.8 is a model schematic and is used only as supporting hydrological context, not as independent proof of the chosen geographic connector.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.mapped_reach_name: Río Cañete on the labeled river continuation

correspondence.component_scope: Vilca, Papacocha and Huancaya lake-and-cascade corridor
correspondence.finding: The MTC originals show the eastward arrival at Vilca and the turn south through the Río Cañete valley to Huancaya. The PROMPERÚ original places Papacocha and Bosque del Amor immediately by Vilca and distinguishes Hualhua on the southward corridor above Huancaya. Its accompanying prose describes the river descending through cascades and lake-like reaches; the MINCETUR records independently describe Papacocha/Bosque del Amor and the connected Huallhua remansos. These are distinct waterbody settings within the selected corridor, not renamed tributaries or lakes.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Vitis, Piquecocha, Alis and Laraos junctions
correspondence.finding: South of Huancaya the selected course continues past Vitis and the Piquecocha setting toward Tinco Alis. The original PROMPERÚ map labels the river and Piquecocha and shows the eastern Río Alis branch through Tomas and Alis meeting the selected north-to-south corridor. The course continues through Llapay; the MTC Lima original distinguishes the eastern Laraos drainage and the westward local tributary valleys from the main selected course.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Huantán, Magdalena/Yauyos and Putinza middle corridor
correspondence.finding: The Lima original continues the same river south from the Llapay sector, showing the Huantán tributary from the east and the Yauyos-side tributary from the west. The selected route stays on the main valley near Magdalena and continues through the Putinza corridor, while the Colonia and high-lake drainages join laterally. This correspondence is established from the source river lines and junction settings rather than a basin label alone.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Capillucas/Chavín, Tupe, Cacra and El Platanal setting
correspondence.finding: The mapped Cañete corridor proceeds south through the Chavín/Capillucas sector toward Catahuasi, where the Tupe branch joins from the east; farther downstream the Cacra branch is separately drawn. The primary 2018 study's station map and table locate the Chavín/Capillucas and restitution settings on this corridor. Its prose identifies the middle-basin Capillucas reservoir, its supply to El Platanal and the restitution reservoir returning water to the Cañete. The selected natural valley line is not replaced by the hydroelectric diversion or given the reservoir's name. Precise contemporary impoundment margins and diversion-operation details are outside scope.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
reservoir_names: Embalse de Capillucas (Capilluca in the study section heading)

correspondence.component_scope: Lower canyon and agricultural valley
correspondence.finding: The original Lima map and retained Ica map follow the southwestward valley past Zúñiga and Pacarán to Lunahuaná, Catapalla and Socsi. Below Ramadilla the San Vicente district original traces the river into the broad lower valley, south of Nuevo Imperial and the main San Vicente urban area. Regional tourism prose corroborates the named Catapalla–Socsi river reach without substituting for the map reading.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual Pacific outlet
correspondence.finding: The San Vicente original labels Río Cañete across the lower valley, shows its passage at the Río Cañete bridge and Puente Henry Aramayo, and carries the watercourse to the Pacific shoreline beside Herbay Bajo and the Boca del Río locality. The terminal is read from actual coastal cartography, not merely the stored sea class, a nearby coastal place name or the downstream endpoint metadata.
